cards.card_text: "You also were with Jesus the Galilean," a servant girl says, walking right up to him.
cards.verse_text: “You also were with Jesus the Galilean,” she said.
cards.snippet: “You also were with Jesus the Galilean,” she said.

cards.verse_text: After a little while, those standing nearby said once more to Peter, “Surely you are one of them, for you too are a Galilean.”
cards.snippet: …Peter, “Surely you are one of them, for you too are a Galilean.”

cards.card_text: Then some people standing there tell Him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate, the governor of Judea (Luke 3:1), had mixed with their sacrifices.
cards.verse_text: At that time some of those present told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
cards.snippet: At that time some of those present told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.

cards.card_text: Jesus hears about the Galileans whose blood Pilate mixed with their sacrifices.
cards.verse_text: To this He replied, “Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered this way?

cards.verse_text: About an hour later, another man insisted, “Certainly this man was with Him, for he too is a Galilean.”

cards.card_text: Pilate catches that one word and asks if the man is a Galilean.

cards.card_text: After Theudas, a man called Judas the Galilean (not Judas Iscariot) drew people after him, and he perished too.
cards.verse_text: After him, Judas the Galilean appeared in the days of the census and drew away people after him.
